title: Tunisia national primary energy production fell 23% between 2010 and 2015 as the full-balance energy deficit more than doubled

rootCauses.cause: The minister attributed the decline mainly to natural field decline and inadequate reserve replacement through discoveries (press-relayed attribution, not a measured decomposition). ONEM's series shows primary production falling each year from 2010 to 2015, so the decline predates Article 13.

In a 2021 hearing as reported by WMC/TAP, the minister attributed reluctance to invest partly to social protests. Oxford Business Group reported three wells drilled by international oil companies in 2015 and cited work stoppages and permit non-renewals. These tier-C reports do not establish an annual investment trend or quantify effects on production.

Article 13 changed the approval process in 2014. The production decline had already begun, and the evidence does not measure how much the approval process contributed to subsequent exploration decisions.

author: TahaGHZ
excerpt: Tunisia moved from an energy surplus to a deficit around 2000-2001. Official charts show the primary balance at "Equilibre" in 2000 and in deficit from 2001. By 2010 Tunisia was already a net energy importer. From 2010…

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content:
Tunisia moved from an energy surplus to a deficit around 2000-2001. Official charts show the
primary balance at "Equilibre" in 2000 and in deficit from 2001 (SRC-TG-141). By 2010 Tunisia was
already a net energy importer. From 2010 to 2015, national primary energy production fell from
8,293 to 6,397 ktep, a computed 22.9% decline, while the full-balance energy-deficit share of gross
inland consumption rose from 19.5% to 41.5% (SRC-TG-130). The same official series records
production of 5,077 ktep and a deficit share of 54.9% in 2019; net energy imports rose from 2.1
Mtep in 2010 to 6.5 Mtep in 2019 (SRC-TG-130). Separate sources report that valid exploration and
research permits fell from 56 in 2010 to 23 at end-2020, according to the minister, while ONEM
counted 25 valid permits at end-March 2020; these are differently dated reported counts, not a
continuous series (SRC-TG-139; SRC-TG-131). The available evidence does not establish that
exploration effort collapsed during 2010-2015.

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content:
The measured problem is declining domestic production and a widening energy deficit. Evidence about
causes is less complete and does not quantify the contribution of geology, investment conditions,
social conflict or approval procedures.

- **Depletion without replacement (technical; minister-attributed).** The minister attributed the
  hydrocarbon-output decline mainly to natural field decline and inadequate reserve replacement
  through discoveries (SRC-TG-139). This is a ministerial explanation relayed by press, not a
  measured decomposition of ONEM's broader primary-energy series. The ONEM full-balance series
  records falling primary production each year from 2010 to 2015, including 7,616 ktep in 2011 and
  7,304 ktep in 2013 (SRC-TG-130). The decline therefore predates Article 13 and cannot have been
  initiated by it; that timing alone does not quantify later effects.
- **Reported investment conditions and social conflict (institutional).** The minister cites
  "la réticence des entreprises à investir, en raison des protestations sociales" (SRC-TG-139). This
  attribution is not an independently measured post-2011 investment trend. OBG reports three wells
  drilled by international oil companies in 2015; this is a single-year count (SRC-TG-138). Its
  account also mentions work stoppages and permit non-renewals, without quantifying their effects.
- **Past decision: Article 13 and the approval regime (policy, legacy).** The 2014 Constitution
  made natural resources the property of the people. It requires investment agreements to go to
  a parliamentary committee and the related conventions to be approved by the Assembly
  (SRC-TG-136). Under the old code, the executive approved conventions by decree and granted or
  renewed permits by ministerial order (SRC-TG-137). In July 2014 the ANC energy committee
  refused to extend three hydrocarbon permits (Borj El Khadra, Baguel, El Franig), according to a press report (SRC-TG-340, tier C).
  OBG's statement that the committee refused renewal of "all" hydrocarbon permits, until Article 13's implementing laws were in
  place, is not supported by that report (SRC-TG-138, tier C). The stated reasons in SRC-TG-340 are alleged legal and financial
  infractions and, for two permits, the operator's 30-year cap argument; the committee record was not located.
  The Hydrocarbons Code amendment was adopted on 18 April 2017. A legal-expert presentation noted permits were
  expiring and others waiting (SRC-TG-137). These sources suggest possible administrative delay, but
  none measures its effect. Article 13 did not initiate the production decline already under way in
  2010-2013; the evidence does not establish whether the new approval regime materially affected
  later exploration or production, and no causal magnitude is assigned.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
- Primary production, full national balance, ktep: 2010 8,293; 2011 7,616; 2012 7,566; 2013
  7,304; 2014 6,749; 2015 6,397; 2019 5,077 (SRC-TG-130, Tableau 7).
- Deficit as share of gross inland consumption: 2010 19.5%; 2012 26.2%; 2014 36.3%; 2015 41.5%;
  2019 54.9% (SRC-TG-130, Tableau 18).
- Crude oil's share of national production fell from 48% to 37% over 2010-2019, and energy
  exports fell 55% (SRC-TG-130).
- On the separate classic monthly-bulletin basis, primary resources were 5,219 ktep in 2015 against
  8,916 ktep of demand (SRC-TG-221). That is an independence rate of about 59% (computed).
- The minister gives 93% energy independence in 2010 and 43% in 2020, with hydrocarbon output of
  7 Mtoe in 2010 and 3.5 Mtoe in 2020 (SRC-TG-139). These are attributed, press-reported statements;
  the source does not specify the independence-index basis. **The sources disagree on the 2010 baseline.**
  ONEM's full balance gives 8.3 Mtep of primary production and a 19.5% deficit (about 80% coverage)
  in 2010 (SRC-TG-130). The minister's 2020 value matches ONEM's classic-approach rate, 43%
  (SRC-TG-133), which counts the Algerian gas royalty as a national resource. His 2010 figure may use a different basis; the article does not say. The two series are not spliced
  here.
- ANME / ONE chart: primary resources of 6,225 ktep against 8,757 ktep of consumption in 2013,
  about 71% coverage (SRC-TG-141, computed). The surplus ended in 2000.
- Permits: 56 in 2010 (SRC-TG-139, tier C) and 25 at end-March 2020 (17 research, 8 prospecting;
  SRC-TG-131).

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content:
Medium. The production and deficit series are official and internally consistent (SRC-TG-130).
The causes rest on weaker ground. Depletion and investor reluctance come from a minister's
statement relayed by the press (SRC-TG-139). The Article 13 link rests on a business publication
(SRC-TG-138) and an expert slide deck (SRC-TG-137). The 2010 permit count has no tier A source.
The magnitude of each cause is unknown. Strictly, the timeframe is `past` for the 2010-2015 shift,
but the decline did not stop in 2015 (see FND-TG-131).

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content:
None found in the sources opened. The production decline feeds the gas shortfall in power
generation described in FND-TG-100 and FND-TG-101. Those findings cover the energy-sector link,
not another sector.

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- 2017 amendment to the Hydrocarbons Code to comply with Article 13, adopted by the ARP on 18 April 2017 (SRC-TG-137): https://tn.boell.org/sites/default/files/afef_marrakchi_-_modification_du_code_des_hydrocarbures.pdf
- Hydrocarbons Code (1999), the regime amended in 2017. Its law number and date were seen only in an unopened IEA policy-database search result.
- Parliamentary approval of individual concession extension agreements, e.g. Gremda, Maamoura and Jebal Doulab in 2021 (SRC-TG-139).
- Article 13, 2014 Constitution: https://www.icnl.org/wp-content/uploads/Tunisia_CONSTITUTION-DE-LA-REPUBLIQUE-TUNISIENNE.pdf

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content:
The ONEM production series establishes the dated decline. Article 13 was adopted after the decline began, and the sources cannot apportion it between resource maturity, investment, disruption and regulation. Reported permit disputes provide context only.

**Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass after corrections. Checked in the original or a local copy: ONEM Bilan energetique 2019 production and deficit tables (SRC-TG-130, Tableau 7 and Tableau 18; net imports 2.1 to 6.5 Mtep in the text), ONEM classic balance 2015 (SRC-TG-221, 5,219 and 8,916 ktep), ONEM March 2020 bulletin permit count (SRC-TG-131, 25 permits), the WMC/TAP report of the minister's statement (SRC-TG-139), and L'Economiste Maghrebin, 10 July 2014 (SRC-TG-340). Correction: the 2014 permit refusal is now stated as three named permits per press, and OBG's "all permits" is recorded as unsupported; the data gap and the outstanding line were updated accordingly. The ANC committee record and the reasons remain unlocated. Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

resolvedSources.title: Evolution du bilan énergétique de la Tunisie 2010-2019 (mise à jour juin 2023)
resolvedSources.publisher: Observatoire National de l'Energie et des Mines (ONEM), Ministère de l'Industrie, des Mines et de l'Energie
resolvedSources.extracts:
PDF p. 9, Résumé exécutif, "Production primaire en baisse":

> La production nationale a baissé de 39% sur la période 2010-2019, soit une moyenne de 5.3%/an. Cette baisse a été observée surtout au niveau du pétrole brut dont la part relative dans la production totale est passée de 48% à 37% en l'espace de 10 ans. La baisse de la production nationale s'est accompagnée d'une baisse des exportations (-55% sur 10 ans équivalent à -8.6%/an en moyenne) et par une croissance de 37% des importations (une moyenne de 3,5%/an).

English gloss: national primary production fell 39% over 2010-2019 (5.3% a year on average),
mainly crude oil, whose share of production fell from 48% to 37%. Exports fell 55% and imports
grew 37% over the period.

PDF p. 10, Résumé exécutif, "Une balance de plus en plus déséquilibrée":

> Ainsi, le déficit énergétique a plus que triplé, soit un accroissement de 209% sur la période et 13.3%/an en moyenne. Le déficit énergétique a changé d'échelle ; grimpant à 55% en 2019, alors qu'il n'était que de 20% en 2010.

English gloss: the energy deficit more than tripled (+209%, 13.3% a year); it reached 55% (of
gross inland consumption) in 2019 against 20% in 2010.

PDF p. 25, section 2.1.1, text and Tableau 7 "Evolution des flux énergétiques sur la période 2010-2019 en Tunisie (ktep)", row "Production primaire":

> la production nationale a baissé passant 8,3 Mtep en 2010 à 5,1 Mtep en 2019 ; soit une régression de 39% sur la période équivalent à 5.3% en moyenne/an.

> Production primaire | 2010: 8 293 | 2011: 7 616 | 2012: 7 566 | 2013: 7 304 | 2014: 6 749 | 2015: 6 397 | 2016: 6 043 | 2017: 5 524 | 2018: 5 396 | 2019: 5 077

English gloss: primary production fell from 8.3 Mtep (2010) to 5.1 Mtep (2019). The yearly row
shows 6,749 ktep in 2014 and 6,397 ktep in 2015.

PDF p. 27, text after Figure 17:

> Face à ce constat, le solde largement importateur net déjà en 2010, a été marqué par une forte hausse ; passant de 2,1 Mtep à 6,5 Mtep ; soit une progression de 210% sur la période.

English gloss: the country was already a large net importer in 2010; net imports rose from
2.1 Mtep to 6.5 Mtep (+210%) by 2019.

PDF p. 50, section 3.1.3 and Tableau 18 "Evolution de la balance énergétique sur la période 2010-2019 en Tunisie (ktep)":

> Déficit énergétique (ktep) | 2010: 2 013 | 2011: 2 180 | 2012: 2 682 | 2013: 3 115 | 2014: 3 844 | 2015: 4 533 | 2016: 4 962 | 2017: 5 831 | 2018: 6 050 | 2019: 6 190
> Déficit énergétique (%) | 2010: 19,5% | 2011: 22,3% | 2012: 26,2% | 2013: 29,9% | 2014: 36,3% | 2015: 41,5% | 2016: 45,1% | 2017: 51,3% | 2018: 52,9% | 2019: 54,9%

Footnote 25: "(Consommation intérieure brute - Production nationale) / Consommation intérieure brute"

English gloss: energy deficit in ktep and as a share of gross inland consumption, 2010-2019.
The deficit ratio is (gross inland consumption minus national production) divided by gross
inland consumption.

PDF p. 51, text under Figure 52:

> A rappeler que ce déficit qui découle du bilan national de l'énergie prend en compte la biomasse, l'autoconsommation du secteur énergétique, le soutage international et la consommation des gazoducs ce qui peut amener à des écarts par rapport à l'approche classique basée sur le bilan d'énergie primaire calculé mensuellement.

English gloss: this deficit comes from the full national energy balance (with biomass, energy
sector own use, international bunkers and pipeline consumption), so it can differ from the
"classic" monthly primary energy balance used in the conjoncture bulletins.

p. 45, text under Figure 46 (agriculture and fishing, 2010-2019) (added for FND-TG-270):

> L'électricité est la deuxième source d'énergie dans ce secteur, elle est utilisée principalement pour le pompage de l'eau pour irrigation à près de 70% et le reste pour l'activité d'élevage. Elle représente entre 17% et 21% de consommation finale dans ce secteur.

English gloss: electricity is the second energy source in agriculture; about 70% of it is used to
pump irrigation water and the rest for livestock. It is 17% to 21% of the sector's final energy
consumption (2010-2019).

PDF p. 9, Résumé exécutif, "Peu d'évolution de la demande totale d'énergie" (added for FND-TG-290/291):

> L'intensité énergétique primaire a diminué d'environ 0.8% /an très loin de l'objectif tracé de 2-3%/an.

English gloss: primary energy intensity fell by about 0.8% a year (2010-2019), far from the
2-3% a year target.

PDF p. 36, section 2.3.2 (final demand by form of energy):

> Notons ici que la demande finale de gaz naturel est impactée essentiellement par 2 facteurs à savoir (i) la quantité de gaz qui transite et par conséquent la quantité consommée par les stations de compression et (ii) la quantité de petcoke utilisée par les cimenteries en substitution au gaz naturel et vice versa.

English gloss: final natural gas demand is driven mainly by (i) gas transit (compressor station
use) and (ii) the amount of petcoke cement plants use in place of natural gas, and vice versa.

PDF p. 40, section 2.3.3.1, Figure 36 "Evolution de la consommation finale du secteur industriel entre 2010 et 2019" (ktep, data labels) and text:

> 2010: 2 035 | 2011: 1 864 | 2012: 2 040 | 2013: 2 071 | 2014: 2 221 | 2015: 2 189 | 2016: 2 141 | 2017: 2 159 | 2018: 2 146 | 2019: 2 104

> L'évolution de la structure de la consommation d'énergie du secteur industriel est marquée par une permutation entre le gaz naturel et les produits pétroliers, quand l'un augmente l'autre diminue ainsi le gap s'élargi et se rétréci en conséquence. Par ailleurs, une tendance vers l'électrification de la demande de l'énergie est remarquable.

English gloss: industrial final energy consumption 2010-2019 in ktep; the industrial fuel mix is
marked by swapping between natural gas and petroleum products, plus a trend to electrification.

PDF p. 47, section 3.1.1:

> Sur la période 2010 et 2019, l'intensité de l'énergie primaire a baissé de l'ordre de 7% passant de 0,234 tep/1000 $ (2010) à 0,219 tep/1000 $ (2010). La baisse annuelle n'a pas dépassé 0,8% en moyenne loin de l'objectif tracé de 3%.

English gloss: primary intensity fell about 7% over 2010-2019, from 0.234 to 0.219 toe per
1,000 USD (2010); the yearly fall did not exceed 0.8% on average, far from the 3% target. (The
executive summary on p. 9 gives the target as 2-3% a year.)

PDF p. 59, section 3.3.1:

> La tendance de l'intensité finale a été marquée par une baisse timide de l'ordre de 5% sur l'ensemble de la période passant de 0,114 tep/1000 DT (2010) à 0,109 tep/1000 DT (2010)

English gloss: final energy intensity of the whole economy fell only about 5% over 2010-2019,
from 0.114 to 0.109 toe per 1,000 TND (2010 prices).

PDF p. 60, section 3.3.2, Tableau 23 "Intensité énergétique de l'industrie" (industry = manufacturing + mining + construction) and text:

> Consommation finale Ind. (ktep) | 2010: 2 035 | 2011: 1 864 | 2012: 2 040 | 2013: 2 071 | 2014: 2 221 | 2015: 2 189 | 2016: 2 141 | 2017: 2 159 | 2018: 2 146 | 2019: 2 104
> VA industrielle (MDT cnst 2010) | 13 637 | 13 062 | 13 341 | 13 631 | 13 861 | 13 737 | 13 855 | 13 977 | 14 057 | 13 994
> Intensité énergétique finale de l'industrie (tep/1000DT) | 0,149 | 0,143 | 0,153 | 0,152 | 0,160 | 0,159 | 0,155 | 0,154 | 0,153 | 0,150

> On constate que l'intensité énergétique finale dans le secteur industriel a eu une tendance plutôt stable avec une légère tendance vers la hausse, entre 2010 et 2019. Ceci peut indiquer que l'industrie tunisienne est légèrement moins efficace de point de vue énergétique.

> Il faut cependant relativiser car l'évolution de l'intensité énergétique dans l'industrie est influencée par deux principaux facteurs à savoir : [...] L'évolution des consommations énergétiques spécifiques au niveau des branches énergivores. Une analyse plus poussée de la tendance de l'intensité par branche industrielle et de la consommation spécifique des industries énergivores sort du cadre de ce travail et fait partie des prérogatives de l'ANME qui le réalise régulièrement. [...] Les changements dans la structure de la valeur ajoutée de l'industrie. La figure qui suit montre qu'il n'y avait pas d'effet structure observable durant la période de l'étude.

PDF p. 61, text beside Figure 66:

> Ainsi, les industries mécaniques et électriques qui ont une très forte valeur ajoutée ne sont pas énergivores et inversement pour les industries des matériaux de construction, céramique et verre.

English gloss: industrial final energy intensity was flat to slightly rising over 2010-2019
(0.149 to 0.150 toe per 1,000 TND, peak 0.160 in 2014); ONEM reads this as Tunisian industry
being slightly less energy-efficient, with the caveats that branch-level specific consumption is
ANME's remit and that no structural effect in value added was observed. High value-added
mechanical and electrical industries use little energy; building materials, ceramics and glass
are the reverse.

PDF pp. 71-80, annex "Bilan national de l'énergie" 2010 to 2019 (one page per year), rows "Industrie" and "Produits minéraux non métalliques", columns "Total tous produits", "PETCOKE", "Gaz Naturel", "Electricité" (ktep):

> Industrie, total: 2010: 2 035 | 2011: 1 864 | 2012: 2 040 | 2013: 2 071 | 2014: 2 221 | 2015: 2 189 | 2016: 2 141 | 2017: 2 159 | 2018: 2 146 | 2019: 2 104
> Industrie, PETCOKE: 2010: 342 | 2011: 295 | 2012: 358 | 2013: 420 | 2014: 574 | 2015: 621 | 2016: 589 | 2017: 547 | 2018: 442 | 2019: 528
> Produits minéraux non métalliques, total: 2010: 965 | 2011: 927 | 2012: 1 074 | 2013: 1 123 | 2014: 1 226 | 2015: 1 225 | 2016: 1 173 | 2017: 1 172 | 2018: 1 130 | 2019: 1 109
> Produits minéraux non métalliques, PETCOKE: same values as Industrie, PETCOKE (all industrial petcoke is in this branch)
> Produits minéraux non métalliques, Gaz Naturel: 2010: 491 | 2011: 497 | 2012: 565 | 2013: 557 | 2014: 499 | 2015: 457 | 2016: 442 | 2017: 486 | 2018: 548 | 2019: 443
> Chimie, total: 2010: 184 | 2011: 137 | 2012: 163 | 2013: 159 | 2014: 183 | 2015: 166 | 2016: 164 | 2017: 172 | 2018: 164 | 2019: 173

English gloss: industrial and non-metallic minerals (cement, lime, bricks, ceramics, glass) final
consumption by fuel. Petcoke was already 342 ktep in 2010 and peaked at 621 ktep in 2015; gas use
in the branch fell from 557 (2013) to 442-457 (2015-2016). Chemicals (which include the phosphate
processing industry) used 137-184 ktep a year.
resolvedSources.notes:
Official retrospective consolidation of the national energy balances (IEA-style methodology).
Its deficit ratio is not the same indicator as the monthly bulletins' "taux d'indépendance
énergétique" (resources over demand, classic approach, with or without the Algerian gas royalty).
The two series must not be spliced. The PDF has a text layer; the table rows above come out
cleanly in pdftotext and add up (production 8,293 and deficit 2,013 against TPES 10,306 in 2010).
Page numbers are PDF page numbers located by text search; printed numbers match.

Note on the annex rows (added for FND-TG-290): the annual balance tables on pp. 71-80 are printed
rotated, so the rows above were rebuilt from word positions in the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF), not
copied from a clean text line. They check out: for each year the non-metallic minerals row equals
petcoke + gas + electricity (+ small biomass/solar), e.g. 2010: 342 + 491 + 128 + 3 = 964 against
965 printed, and the Industrie totals match Tableau 23 on p. 60.

resolvedSources.title: Constitution de la République tunisienne (27 janvier 2014), texte français
resolvedSources.publisher: Assemblée nationale constituante (text hosted by the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law, ICNL)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article 13:

> Les ressources naturelles appartiennent au peuple tunisien. L'État y exerce sa souveraineté en son nom.
> Les accords d'investissement relatifs à ces ressources sont soumis à la commission spéciale de l'Assemblée des représentants du peuple. Les conventions y afférentes sont soumises à l'approbation de l'Assemblée.

English gloss: natural resources belong to the Tunisian people; the State exercises
sovereignty over them in the people's name. Investment agreements on these resources go to
the competent committee of the Assembly of the Representatives of the People, and the related
conventions are submitted to the Assembly for approval.
resolvedSources.notes:
Primary legal text, but this copy is a French version hosted by an NGO, not the Journal
Officiel. The UNDP/International IDEA English translation on constituteproject.org
(https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Tunisia_2014) was also opened and matches in
substance. `type` uses official-statistics because the template has no "legal text" value.
The 2014 Constitution was replaced in 2022; whether the 2022 text keeps a parliamentary
approval rule for resource contracts was not checked.

resolvedSources.title: Modification (Réforme) du Code des Hydrocarbures (presentation)
resolvedSources.publisher: Afef Hammami Marrakchi (doctor of law), hosted by Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung Tunis
resolvedSources.extracts:
Slide "ARP: Projet de réforme, Exposé des motifs du projet":

> Modifier le code pour le rendre conforme , compatible avec les dispositions de l'article 13 de la Constitution , renforcement du rôle du pouvoir législatif en matière de ressources naturelles au regard du pouvoir dominant de l'exécutif en la matière

> Ou sont les autres articles ? Pourquoi en plusieurs étapes? Le temps presse / permis qui expirent/perms qui attendent/ revoir le plutôt le régime d'approbation

English gloss: the bill's stated purpose was to bring the Hydrocarbons Code into line with
Article 13 and strengthen the legislature's role. The author asks why only some articles were
changed, noting that time is short, with permits expiring and permits waiting, and that the
approval regime should be reviewed.

Slide "La commission industrie, énergie, ressources naturelles, infrastructure et environnement, Rapport":

> Justifications Conformité de code avec l'article 13 ( d'après le code pouvoir exécutif en matière d'approbation des conventions particulières d'exploration/recherche et d'exploitation par décret, ainsi qu'en matière d'octroi et de renouvellement des permis y afférents par arrêté du ministre chargé des hydrocarbures

> Mardi 18 avril 2017, le projet de loi relatif à l'amendement d'un nombre de dispositions du code des hydrocarbures est adopté.

English gloss: before the amendment, the code let the executive approve exploration and
production conventions by decree and grant or renew permits by ministerial order. The bill
amending several provisions of the Hydrocarbons Code was adopted on Tuesday 18 April 2017.
resolvedSources.notes:
Slide deck by a legal academic for a Böll Foundation event; undated (content refers to events
of April-May 2017, so 2017 or later). It is an expert's analysis, not an official record, and
gives no figures on permit numbers or delays. The law number and JORT reference of the 2017
amendment were not found in an opened source.

resolvedSources.title: All change: A new law to increase government review of energy contracts promises wide-reaching effects for the industry (The Report: Tunisia 2016)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article text:

> requiring parliamentary approval for energy contracts may have an impact on the sector's overall investment attractiveness, increasing scope for politicisation.

> Tunisia imported an estimated 51% of its gas from Algeria in 2014 – that number rose to 54% by 2015, a year in which only three wells were drilled by international oil companies. Domestic oil production has dropped around 10% per year and, according to Tunisian press reports, some upstream companies – such as the UK's Enquest – are leaving the country due a range of issues, from work stoppages to the non-renewal of drilling permits.

> In 2014 the energy committee refused renewal of all hydrocarbons permits, emphasising that Article 13 and its attached laws and by-laws must be completed first in order to proceed in an ethical and legal manner.

English gloss (en source): parliamentary approval may reduce investment attractiveness; only
three wells were drilled by international oil companies in 2015; some operators were leaving
over work stoppages and non-renewal of permits; in 2014 the energy committee refused to renew
all hydrocarbon permits until Article 13's implementing laws were in place.
resolvedSources.notes:
Business-intelligence publisher; partly based on press reports and does not cite primary
documents for the 2014 refusal or the well count. The "51%/54% of gas from Algeria" figures are
not used here; ONEM data are preferred.

resolvedSources.title: La Tunisie ne compte plus que 23 permis de recherche et d'exploration
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article, 26 March 2021:

> Le nombre total de permis de recherche et d'exploration est passé de 56 en 2010 à 23 à fin 2020, a indiqué le ministre de l'Industrie, de l'Energie et des Mines par intérim, Mohamed Boussaid, jeudi 25 mars 2021, lors d'une séance d'audition à la Commission de l'industrie, de l'énergie, des ressources naturelles, et de infrastructure à l'Assemblée des représentants du peuple

English gloss: the acting minister told the parliamentary energy committee on 25 March 2021
that the number of exploration and research permits fell from 56 in 2010 to 23 at end-2020.

> Boussaid a fait état, aussi, de la régression de la production nationale des hydrocarbures, passant de 7 millions de tonnes équivalent pétrole (Tep) en 2010 à 3,5 millions de tep, soit une baisse d'environ 50%. D'après lui, cette chute est due principalement au déclin naturel des champs de production, et au manque de renouvellement du stock national via la découverte de nouveaux champs, ainsi que la réticence des entreprises à investir, en raison des protestations sociales.

English gloss: hydrocarbon production fell from 7 Mtoe in 2010 to 3.5 Mtoe (about -50%). He
attributed this mainly to natural field decline, failure to replace reserves through new
discoveries, and companies' reluctance to invest because of social protests.

> « La régression des indicateurs d'exploration et de production d'hydrocarbures s'est reflétée directement sur l'indice d'indépendance énergétique, lequel est passé de 93% en 2010 à 43% en 2020 », a-t-il ajouté.

English gloss: the energy independence index fell from 93% in 2010 to 43% in 2020.
resolvedSources.notes:
Press report of a ministerial statement to parliament (TAP wire). Tier C: the hearing minutes
were not found. The 2020 independence value (43%) matches ONEM (SRC-TG-133), suggesting the
minister used the classic bulletin approach with the gas royalty counted as a resource. His
2010 figures (93% independence, 7 Mtoe hydrocarbons) are on a different basis from ONEM's full
energy balance (8.3 Mtep primary production, 19.5% deficit in 2010, SRC-TG-130). The 56-permit
figure for 2010 has no tier A confirmation.

resolvedSources.title: Tunisie - permis pétroliers refusés
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article, 10 July 2014:

> Il s'agit des permis «Borj El Khadra», «Baguel» (Douz) et «El Franig» (Médenine).

English gloss: the permits concerned are Borj El Khadra, Baguel (Douz) and El Franig (Médenine).

> En raison des infractions légales et financières, l'adoption des trois projets de loi

English gloss: because of legal and financial infractions, the adoption of the three draft laws (on extending the research permits) was rejected by the energy committee of the National Constituent Assembly. The article gives different reasons by permit: infractions over a 23-year period for Borj El Khadra; for Baguel and El Franig, the operator Perenco invoked the 1985 decree's 30-year cap, so its 15-year extension request was not admissible.
